summary: Markets, earnings, central banks, M&A deals, commodities, and credit events. The story is the move with its number, not the political framing of it.
fits_when: primary_entities includes a public company, central bank, currency, sovereign issuer, or major index
key_points OR structured_numbers contains a price / rate / yield / volume / earnings figure with a unit
the load-bearing claim is a number with a unit (price, %, basis points, share count)
fits_poorly_when: story is principally about a regulator's *new rule* rather than a market reaction (use policy)
story is principally about a state-level sanctions or treaty action with market secondary effects (use geopolitics)
story is a tech product launch where price is incidental (use tech)

numbers_discipline.comparator_window_required: every percentage move must include the comparator window (single-day, since-IPO, year-to-date, prior-meeting)
precision_rules: use the figure exactly as in 02_evidence.numeric_facts
round only when the rounded value is also in numeric_facts (with context: 'rounded for narration')
always include the unit ($, %, bps, M shares)
numbers_discipline.as_of_required: every quoted figure must have an as_of date or session reference (e.g., 'at the close Tuesday', 'after the FOMC decision')
numbers_discipline.conflicts_must_surface: if sources disagree on a figure (DOJ filing $10B vs NYT $8B), both numbers appear with attribution — never resolve silently

preferred_pattern.describes: the headline number with comparator window
the affected counterparty (households, suppliers, holders, savers) with a count
the cause — the announcement, decision, or release that drove the move
the comparison — prior level, prior period, peer group, or benchmark
the next data print, earnings date, or central-bank decision

notes: Data module is the workhorse — most evidence beats reference a numeric_fact_id.
Quote modules from CFOs / central bank chairs are valuable when 02_evidence.quotes carries verbatim transcript text.
Map modules are rare for finance; only useful for commodity flow stories or sovereign-debt geographies.

asset_hint_policy.data: the default for finance — every numeric beat is a data module with numeric_fact_ref set
asset_hint_policy.mute: use when the spoken narration is the asset (e.g., a CEO's statement that doesn't lend itself to a chart)
asset_hint_policy.map: rare; only for commodity flow stories (oil routes, grain exports) or sovereign-debt geography
asset_hint_policy.photo: permitted only when 02_evidence references a specific image source (e.g., a press conference still from a named pool); never stock trading-floor footage

banned_visual_patterns.why: Generic; says nothing about the specific story; visual filler
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Data module with the actual numeric_fact

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Bull / bear icons or animated arrows that decorate without informing
Skyline of Wall Street / City of London / generic financial district
banned_visual_patterns.why: Editorial association with no specific tie to the story
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Mute; let the spoken narration carry

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Stock photo of a CEO not named in the story
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Mute or data; only use a CEO image when (a) they are the named subject AND (b) 02_evidence references a specific photo source
Data module showing the actual figure

banned_visual_patterns.pattern: Red-or-green saturated background overlay tied to direction
banned_visual_patterns.why: Editorialises through palette; small color cue is fine, full overlay is not
banned_visual_patterns.fix: Reserve red strictly for the magnitude label of a decline (e.g., '−8.4%')

lead_with: the SEC filing (10-Q, 10-K, 8-K) or equivalent home-jurisdiction filing
the central bank statement or release
the exchange-published settlement or volume data
the official press release from the issuer
second_tier: Bloomberg / Reuters / FT reporting that quotes the filing or release
WSJ / Economist analysis when the news IS the analysis
treat_with_caution: sell-side analyst notes (use the source, not the desk's framing)
anonymous bankers / 'people familiar with the matter'
social media posts from non-verified accounts
must_cite_explicitly: every percentage with its comparator window
every dollar / euro / yen figure with its date
every basis-point move with the prior level
every named index or rate with its issuer

patterns.name: single-day-move
patterns.shape: <ticker/name> closed <up/down> <pct> on <day> — its largest single-day move since <prior-period>.
patterns.example: Nvidia closed up 8.4% on Tuesday — its largest single-day move since March.

patterns.name: central-bank-decision
patterns.shape: The <body> held/cut/raised rates at <level> for a <ordinal> consecutive meeting.
patterns.example: The Fed held rates at 4.50% for a fifth consecutive meeting.

patterns.name: crossover
patterns.shape: <benchmark> crossed <level> for the first time since <date>.
patterns.example: Brent crossed $90 a barrel for the first time since November 2023.

patterns.name: earnings-beat-miss
patterns.shape: <company> reported <metric> of <value>, <above/below> the street consensus of <consensus>.
patterns.example: Apple reported services revenue of $26.1 billion, above the street consensus of $25.4 billion.

patterns.name: deal-close
patterns.example: Capital One agreed to buy Discover for $35.3 billion in stock on Monday.

first_4_words_must_contain: a public company / central bank / currency / index proper name
banned_constructions: 'In a wild day for markets...' generic openers

good: Nvidia closed up 8.4% on Tuesday — its largest single-day move since March.
The Fed held rates at 4.50% for a fifth consecutive meeting.
Brent crossed $90 a barrel for the first time since November 2023.
Capital One agreed to buy Discover for $35.3 billion in stock on Monday.
bad: Could the Fed surprise the market this week?
In a wild day for tech stocks, Nvidia surged.
Markets are reacting to record-shattering earnings.

subtitle_guidance.L1_role: the headline number with sign and unit
L1_rules: ticker or short proper name leads
L2_rules: always include the comparator window for a percentage move
always include the as-of for a level
L3_rules: name the data source explicitly (exchange, filing, central bank)
if quoting a wire, format as 'Reuters · FOMC statement'
type_specific_rules: Tickers in L1 use uppercase exchange notation (NVDA, AAPL, MSFT).
Percentages render with the sign always ('+8.4%' not '8.4%' for upward moves).
Basis points render as 'bps' not 'basis points' in subtitles (full word in spoken script).

module_selection_hints.include_data_when: ANY numeric beat — which is most of finance; aim for 2-3 data modules per video
module_selection_hints.include_quote_when: 02_evidence.quotes has a verbatim line from a CEO, CFO, or central-bank chair
module_selection_hints.include_map_when: the story is about commodity flow geography or a sovereign-debt event tied to specific countries — rare
module_selection_hints.stakes_module_must_name: the affected counterparty (households on adjustable-rate mortgages, suppliers, equity holders, savers) with a count or comparator

anti_patterns.why: No frame of reference; the comparator is what makes the move newsworthy
anti_patterns.fix: Add 'today's session' / 'since the open' / 'its largest single-day move since <month>'

anti_patterns.why: Records are often disputed by definition; check factual_conflicts and prior series
anti_patterns.fix: If 02_evidence.factual_conflicts touches the record claim, surface both views; otherwise attribute to the issuer's claim

anti_patterns.pattern: Treating a price move as a story
anti_patterns.shape: Hook is just 'Stock X moved Y%'
anti_patterns.why: Markets move every day; the story is the cause or the consequence
anti_patterns.fix: Hook leads with the cause (announcement, ruling, data print) or the consequence (margin call, sector contagion); the move is the L1, not the whole story

anti_patterns.shape: Stakes points at 'investors' as the affected population
anti_patterns.why: Banned generic population; investors aren't a stakes-bearing population in a 60s explainer
anti_patterns.fix: Name the real counterparty: '30 million ARM-mortgage households', 'Boeing's 12,000 suppliers', 'sovereign holders of Russian debt'

anti_patterns.pattern: Sell-side analyst note quoted as primary source
anti_patterns.why: Analyst notes are commentary on the source; quote the source itself
anti_patterns.fix: Cite the SEC filing / central-bank statement / earnings release; an analyst note is L3-tier sourcing at best

anti_patterns.shape: Photo asset of NYSE / LSE trading floor

anti_patterns.pattern: Close that hedges harder than the rest of the script
anti_patterns.why: Banned vague forward look; weakest part of finance scripts
anti_patterns.fix: Close anchors on the next print: 'CPI lands Wednesday at 8:30 ET', 'Apple reports November 7', 'FOMC decision December 12'

anti_patterns.shape: Saying 'Google reported' when the ticker is GOOGL/Alphabet
anti_patterns.why: Imprecision; matters for filings and ticker subtitles
anti_patterns.fix: Match the entity to the issuing filing; if Alphabet filed, the issuer is Alphabet

stage_2_extra_checks: every numeric_fact must have unit and as_of (already schema-enforced; verify substantively)
if a percentage move is in numeric_facts, the comparator window must be in 'context' (e.g., 'single-day move', 'YTD')
if the story has an earnings beat/miss, the consensus number must also be in numeric_facts as a separate entry
stage_5_extra_checks: scan 03_script.md for any percentage figure not followed by a comparator phrase ('today', 'this week', 'YTD', 'since <date>', 'consecutive')
verify every numeric beat in the script has a corresponding numeric_fact_ref on its module
verify stakes module names a counterparty other than 'investors' or 'markets'
verify close anchors on a date or scheduled event
